text: Maxi Gnauck (born 10 October 1964) is a German former artistic gymnast who represented East Germany. She earned a total of 27 medals at the Olympic Games, World Championships, World Cups, and European Championships, making her one of the most successful female gymnasts Germany has ever produced. In 1980, she was awarded East German Sportspersonality of the Year. Her parents had planned to name their child Max, but when the baby was a girl, they added an 'i', resulting in the uncommon name Maxi for Germany. When Maxi was five, her mother enrolled her in a gymnastics center in their area. By age eight, she won her first medals at the Kreisspartakiade. At nine, she transferred to SC Dynamo Berlin, where she was coached by Jürgen Heritz. She is regarded as one of the best uneven bars competitors of all time and was also an outstanding tumbler; she was one of the first female gymnasts to perform a triple twist on floor. In April 1986, Maxi officially announced her retirement and began a four-year course in sports coaching at the University of Leipzig. In 1988, she suffered a severe injury while sliding down a waterslide during her work as an aide at a children's summer camp by the Baltic Sea, breaking her C5 vertebra and nearly becoming paralysed; three vertebrae were later reinforced with a metal plate. After the reunification of East Germany and West Germany, facing strong competition, she took temporary coaching positions in South Africa and Great Britain, both for a few months in 1990. From 1993 until 2004, she worked as a full-time coach at the Harksheide Gymnastics Center in Norderstedt near Hamburg. Since 2005, she has worked at the Artistic and Apparatus Gymnastics Center (Kunst- und Gerätturnzentrum) in Liestal, Switzerland. In 2000, she was inducted into the International Gymnastics Hall of Fame, becoming the first German gymnast to receive this honour.
